suggestions.title: run_builds and watch_todos check the project's team after work has already been done, so a mismatched todo now fails halfway
suggestions.failurePath: On a server with more than one team, a todo can have teamId A while its projectId points to a project in team B. Before this PR, chief and MCP create_todo did not check the project's team, so such rows can exist. When chief A calls run_builds on that todo, requireTeamTodo passes, and startBuilds (builds.ts:647, which checks no team) inserts the build, enqueues a step and moves the todo to queued. Only then does requireProjectRow(db, row.projectId, ctx.teamId) at line 831 throw 404. The chief gets 'run_builds rejected: 404 project ...' while a build is in fact running and no auto-watch was added; a retry then fails with 409 (queued to queued). watch_todos (lines 959-961) has the same shape: record.teamId matches, the project's team does not, and the 404 is thrown partway through the loop, after the earlier ids were already watched. Before this PR neither path threw for these rows. Fix: read the project row (or its name) before startBuilds or before the watch loop begins, so the call is rejected before it changes anything.

suggestions.title: Delivered-PR check still reads the raw githubRepo column, while the CI poller now skips that project
suggestions.failurePath: A project's stored githubRepo is 'owner/..' (allowed by the old validator) and a build step finishes with a prNumber. deliveredGithubPr at line 1694 only checks repoKind and githubRepo !== null, so it is true and the todo stays in building. createCiPoller.pollOne (ci-loop.ts:212) now gets null from githubRepoOfProject and counts the build as skipped on every sweep. The task stays in building until someone moves it by hand. The PR's Risk section names this. It is not a regression: before the change, the rewritten request URL returned 404 and was counted as unreadable on every sweep, with the same stuck result. Using githubRepoOfProject at line 1694 as well would send such builds straight to review, matching how the other read paths treat an invalid stored value.

suggestions.title: The closing keyword is only in the second of five commits; the squash-message procedure in CLAUDE.md would drop it
suggestions.evidence: `closes #1466` is only in 18ca807. PR commit order over REST is 1bf7c28 (shared, 'Part of #1466'), 18ca807 (closes), then three docs commits. CLAUDE.md says to take the squash subject and body from `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/<n>/commits -q '.[0].commit.message'`, which yields 1bf7c28's message. The PR body's own 'Squash with this message' block carries the keyword, but its subject keeps the placeholder `(#<this PR>)` instead of (#1468).
suggestions.failurePath: Suppose a merger follows the CLAUDE.md .[0] procedure for the squash body. The commit on main then carries only 'Part of #1466', and #1466 stays OPEN. If the merger pastes the PR body block verbatim instead, main gets the subject suffix '(#<this PR>)'. The repo default (squash body = COMMIT_MESSAGES, title = PR title) avoids both problems. Fix: either put the closing line in the first commit or name the exact squash message, and replace the placeholder with #1468.

suggestions.title: Open #1467 and #1461 split project.githubRepo outside githubRepoOfProject
suggestions.evidence: The commit message and PR body say githubRepoOfProject is the one place the server splits a stored project.githubRepo for an API request. Open PR #1467 adds services/github-reads.ts openTarget, which does `slug?.split('/')` plus its own isGithubRepoRef check and its own `.`/`..` check. Open PR #1461 adds services/issue-intake.ts, which checks isGithubRepoRef(githubRepo) and splits on its own. This is the docs/pr-review.md semantic-conflict check.
suggestions.failurePath: No security regression: #1467 checks dot segments itself, and #1461 gets the check through isGithubRepoRef once this PR merges. But whichever of these PRs merges after #1468 leaves a second split point, and the 'one place' claim stops being true. Whoever merges second should route those reads through githubRepoOfProject.

suggestions.title: builds.ts still decides 'wait for CI' from the raw githubRepo column while the poller now skips invalid repos; R7 asserts the stuck 'building' state as correct
suggestions.failurePath: Project row stored before the fix with githubRepo = 'owner/..'. A build step reports done with prNumber set. deliveredGithubPr at builds.ts:1693 tests only `repoKind === 'github' && githubRepo !== null`, so it is true and the task stays in 'building'. The CI poller (ci-loop.ts:212) now gets null from githubRepoOfProject and skips the candidate on every sweep. No path moves the task to review, so it stays in building forever. apps/server/test/github-repo-dot-segments.test.ts:313 (R7) asserts phase 'building' after the sweep, which encodes this state as expected. No test covers the builds.ts gate with an invalid stored repo. This is hard to reach (the clone of such a repo fails, and the head daemon skips the PR probe), and the PR's Risk section names it. Using githubRepoOfProject at builds.ts:1693 too, with a test that delivery goes straight to review, would make the two judgements agree.
suggestions.evidence: builds.ts:1693-1694 `buildRow.prNumber !== null && projRow?.repoKind === 'github' && projRow.githubRepo !== null`; ci-loop.ts:212 `const repoRef = githubRepoOfProject(projRow)`; github-repo-dot-segments.test.ts:313 `expect(todoRow?.phase).toBe('building')`

suggestions.title: run_builds now runs the team-scoped requireProjectRow after startBuilds has already started builds; no test covers run_builds
suggestions.failurePath: Multi-team server with a team-A todo whose projectId is a team-B project. The pre-fix chief or MCP create_todo could create exactly this row, and it is the anomaly this ticket closes. Chief run_builds passes requireTeamTodo, then startBuilds (chief-tools.ts:817) creates the builds. Next, requireProjectRow(db, row.projectId, ctx.teamId) at :831 throws 404, so the tool reports failure even though the builds are running, and the auto-watch is never added. Chief may then retry and start duplicate builds. watch_todos (:961) has the same throw-after-partial-progress shape for such a todo. project-team-guard.test.ts has no run_builds case, and no mutation targets this call site. This cannot happen on a single-team server. Either check the project before startBuilds, or skip the watch instead of throwing, and add a test.
suggestions.evidence: chief-tools.ts:815-831: `const row = requireTeamTodo(...)`; `const builds = startBuilds(...)`; `started.push(...builds)`; `const projectName = requireProjectRow(db, row.projectId, ctx.teamId).name;`

suggestions.title: One of the three assertions in the new daemon probe case passes on origin/main as well
suggestions.failurePath: `githubRepoRefOf('https://github.com/../user.git')` gives null with or without the fix, because new URL() rewrites the path to '/user.git', which is a single segment and fails the slash check. The case still fails on main through the two repo-segment assertions (`owner/...git` and `owner/..git`); mutation M1 confirms this. So the case discriminates, but this line adds no coverage and its comment suggests it guards stored '../user' rows. The only consequence is a misleading assertion.
suggestions.evidence: github-probe.test.ts:157-159 and github-probe.ts:33-42 (new URL(cloneUrl).pathname, then isGithubRepoRef)

suggestions.title: chief run_builds checks the project's team only after startBuilds has run
suggestions.failurePath: Setup: a multi-team server holds a todo whose teamId is A and whose projectId is a team-B project. Before this PR, chief or MCP create_todo could make such a row, since requireProjectRow did not check the team. When team A's chief calls run_builds on that todo, requireTeamTodo passes (todo.teamId == A) and startBuilds({projectId: <team B project>}) at line 819 creates and enqueues builds against team B's project. Only then does the new requireProjectRow(db, row.projectId, ctx.teamId) at line 831 throw 404. Result: the cross-team build already exists and is dispatched, while the tool reports an error and adds no watch. The new team check is placed where it cannot stop the action it should guard. Moving the requireProjectRow call ahead of startBuilds makes it a real guard. This needs pre-existing mismatched rows on a server with more than one team, so it is not blocking.
suggestions.evidence: chief-tools.ts at head lines 817-831: `const row = requireTeamTodo(db, todoId, ctx.teamId); const builds = startBuilds(..., { projectId: row.projectId, ... }); started.push(...builds); const projectName = requireProjectRow(db, row.projectId, ctx.teamId).name;`

suggestions.title: todos-tool team filter goes beyond the ticket's stated scope
suggestions.failurePath: Ticket #1466 scopes the team fix to the two requireProjectRow sites and their callers (MCP create_todo; chief docs, create_todo, update_project, connect_repo). The PR also changes the chief and MCP `todos` tools (chief-tools.ts:268, mcp-face.ts:191). Those tools never called requireProjectRow, and now always AND the caller's team with projectId. The effect is a tightening: another team's projectId lists [] instead of that team's todos, and same-team behavior is unchanged. Mutations M6/M7 and live.txt cover it, and the PR body states it, but it is a behavior change on the protected file mcp-face.ts that the ticket did not ask for. suggestions.evidence: mcp-face.ts:191 `let records = listTodos(svc, { teamId: ctx.teamId, ...(projectId ? { projectId } : {}) });` (was `projectId ? { projectId } : { teamId: ctx.teamId }`). Ticket scope: 「两处 requireProjectRow 加 teamId」
